properties.decision: SETTLED (a) ON ANTHONY'S WORD, 2026-08-16. `valid_from` and `valid_to` become DECLARED date-string properties on TemporalFact, and the readers prefer the `VALID_FROM` / `VALID_TO` EDGE where one exists and fall back to the property where one does not. The edge remains the richer statement; the property stops being a silent no-op.
properties.name: A fact may carry its date as a property — the edge stays the truth when there is an epoch, and the property is read when there is not
properties.rationale:
MEASURED FIRST, DECIDED SECOND. 112 of 205 TemporalFacts carried a `valid_from` PROPERTY the schema did not declare and no code read; 76 carried the declared EDGE to a DesignEpoch; ZERO carried both; 17 carried neither. Full measurement in `fact:defect-half-the-temporal-facts-date-themselves-where-nothing-reads`.

⭐ THE ZERO OVERLAP IS WHAT DECIDED IT. Two populations with two conventions and no node caught between them is not sloppiness — sloppiness would be mixed. It is a MISSING WORD: `VALID_FROM` demands a DesignEpoch, and a writer holding a plain date has nothing to point it at. Everyone who had an epoch used the edge; everyone who had a date invented a property. The corpus was telling the schema what the schema was missing.

WHY (b) LOST — keep the edge as the only truth and migrate the 112. It needs 112 DesignEpochs that do not exist, one per calendar date, which floods the time axis with points that mark nothing. That damages the half of the system that WORKS: the roadmap computation reads epochs, and filling that axis with calendar noise makes it worse, not better. Epochs are meant to be named moments. It also cannot fully clean up, because a property once written cannot be removed (`fact:defect-a-property-once-written-cannot-be-removed`).

WHY (c) LOST — let `VALID_FROM` point at either an epoch or a date. It keeps one word for one idea, which is attractive, but nothing else in this schema has a polymorphic `to`, and the edge-endpoint guard would carry a permanent special case. A lasting complexity cost for a cosmetic win.

WHY (a) SURVIVED THE `dec:edge-orthogonality` OBJECTION, which is the one that mattered. "Two ways to say one thing" is exactly what that decision argues against — but its test is whether a COMPUTATION READS THE DISTINCTION, and here one would. "True from this named milestone" and "true from this date" are different claims: a roadmap wants the first, an audit trail wants the second. The distinction earns its keep.

AND IT IS THE ONLY OPTION THAT DESTROYS NOTHING. 112 hand-written dates become readable immediately; nothing migrates; nothing is invented.

⚠️ A CONFLICT OF INTEREST DISCLOSED BEFORE THE RULING AND RECORDED HERE: the agent proposing this had written a share of those 112 the same day, and therefore had a mild stake in the option that says they were fine. Anthony was told this when the options were put to him and chose (a) anyway.

CARRIED FORWARD, NOT PART OF THE RULING: TemporalFact's extraction_hint reads "a satisfaction fact whose VALID_FROM is a later epoch; a dropped requirement = a fact with VALID_TO set" — phrasing that invited the property form the schema did not declare. The guidance and the schema disagreed and the guidance is what a writer reads, so it is corrected under this decision regardless of which option had won.
